Converts points to a raster: the cell of each point gets its value, the others are novalue.

**Toolbox folder:** Raster Processing<br>
**Status:** Certified<br>
**Keywords:** Raster, Vector, Points, Rasterize<br>
**Authors:** Andrea Antonello<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.modules.PointsRasterizer`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inVector` | vector file |  |  | The points to rasterize. |
| `fCat` | String |  |  | The optional numeric field of the points with the value of their cells. |
| `pCat` | double |  | `1.0` | The value of the cells if no field is given. |
| `inRaster` | raster file |  |  | An optional raster that gives the grid, instead of bounds, resolution and reference system. |
| `pNorth` | Double |  |  | The boundary north coordinate. |
| `pSouth` | Double |  |  | The boundary south coordinate. |
| `pWest` | Double |  |  | The boundary west coordinate. |
| `pEast` | Double |  |  | The boundary east coordinate. |
| `pXres` | Double |  |  | The resolution in x. |
| `pYres` | Double |  |  | The resolution in y. |
| `pCode` | CRS code |  |  | The code defining the coordinate reference system, composed by authority and code number (ex. EPSG:4328). |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outRaster` | output file |  | The rasterized points. |

**Notes**

Each point gives its value to the cell that contains it; the points on the border of two cells go to the one east or south of it, the ones on the east or south border of the grid to its last column or row, and the ones outside of the grid are left out. When more points fall in the same cell, the cell keeps the largest value. The rasterized points, as 1 where there is a point, give their density through KernelDensity; to interpolate the values of the points on all the cells, SurfaceInterpolator is the tool.

The value of the cells is the one of the numeric field of the point, or the constant category without a field. The grid is the one of the optional raster, or the one of the bounds, resolution and reference system.
